title: Stop --recheck resetting the 90-day freshness clock on fully pinned files
description: Pinning moves currency onto the 90-day freshness gate the weekly schedule enforces via --max-age-days 90 against last_checked. But --recheck advances last_checked, and re-fetching a commit-pinned permalink is guaranteed to succeed and proves nothing about currency, so repeatedly rechecking a fully pinned file could reset the freshness clock forever and silently defeat the gate. Not currently reachable: the weekly workflow runs the read-only content test, never --recheck, which is a manual repair tool. Proposed guard: --recheck refuses to advance last_checked when every admitted source in the file is commit-pinned, and says why; a mixed file may still advance on the strength of its live sources. Touches scripts/, so it needs an owner APPROVE TRUST ROOT round.

title: Decide how Dependabot action bumps clear the trust-root gate
description: Every Dependabot github-actions bump edits .github/workflows/*, which is trust root per CONFORMANCE.md line 38, so validate-workflow-policy.py fails it with 'protected trust-root inventory or bytes differ from the trusted base without exact OWNER approval' unless an OWNER posts 'APPROVE TRUST ROOT <head_sha>'. Dependabot cannot obtain that, and the comment is invalidated by its next force-push, so these PRs are permanently red by design rather than by defect. Observed on PR #151 (actions/setup-node 7.0.0->7.1.0 and actions/upload-artifact 7.0.1->7.0.2), run 39229002451, which failed the policy gate before reaching any test. This is NOT the same failure as PR #152, whose Trusted evidence checks failure (run 38345548760) was the STATUS.md clock-dependence defect fixed on branch claude/vigilant-mayer-8ii5g1. Options, all owner decisions: approve each actions bump by hand as it arrives; drop the github-actions ecosystem from dependabot.yml and bump actions deliberately instead; or carve a narrower rule that admits a pinned-SHA-only change to an otherwise byte-identical workflow, which weakens the gate and needs its own threat read. Touches the trust root either way, so whichever option wins needs an owner APPROVE TRUST ROOT round. Surfaced while triaging the open-PR list on 2026-10-23.

title: Decide how Dependabot bumps clear the trust-root gate
description: Dependabot cannot land any bump that edits a REQUIRED_TRUST_ROOT_FILES entry. validate-workflow-policy.py rejects it with 'protected trust-root inventory or bytes differ from the trusted base without exact OWNER approval' unless an OWNER posts 'APPROVE TRUST ROOT <head_sha>', which Dependabot cannot obtain and which its next force-push invalidates. These PRs are red by design, not by defect. SCOPE IS WIDER THAN GITHUB ACTIONS: it covers the root pip ecosystem too, because pyproject.toml and tests/requirements.txt are both protected. Affected open PRs as of 2026-10-23: #151 (.github/workflows/pattern-validation.yml, two action bumps, run 39229002451), #140 and #141 (pyproject.toml + tests/requirements.txt), #142 and #143 (tests/requirements.txt). Reproduced deterministically offline: two checkouts of main, apply only the #140 idna 3.19->3.20 bump to the candidate, and the gate fails naming both files, while an untouched candidate passes. So a one-line pinned dependency bump is indistinguishable to the gate from a trust-root attack, which is the point of the gate and also why nothing automated can satisfy it. NOT the same failure as #144, #145 and #152, which touch no protected file and fail only the STATUS.md clock-dependence defect fixed on branch claude/vigilant-mayer-8ii5g1; #152 is confirmed in run 38345548760, the other two were last validated 2026-09-21 before the 90-day boundary and are expected to fail the same way if revalidated. Options, all owner decisions: approve each bump by hand as it arrives; narrow the Dependabot ecosystems so it stops proposing changes it can never land, and bump those pins deliberately instead; or admit a version-only change to an otherwise byte-identical protected manifest, which weakens the gate against a malicious pin and needs its own threat read before anyone writes it. Whichever wins touches the trust root and needs its own APPROVE TRUST ROOT round. Reworded 2026-10-23 after classifying all eight open Dependabot PRs; the first line of this task described only the github-actions case.

title: Decide how Dependabot bumps clear the trust-root gate
description: Dependabot cannot land any bump that edits a REQUIRED_TRUST_ROOT_FILES entry. validate-workflow-policy.py rejects it with 'protected trust-root inventory or bytes differ from the trusted base without exact OWNER approval' unless an OWNER posts 'APPROVE TRUST ROOT <head_sha>', which Dependabot cannot obtain and which its next force-push invalidates. CLOSED 2026-10-23: owner chose the narrowing option. .github/dependabot.yml now sets open-pull-requests-limit: 0 for github-actions at / and for pip at /, /.github and /tests, which stops version updates for every directory holding a protected manifest while leaving security updates on their separate internal limit of ten.
